senses.def: measuring a great distance from one end to the other
examples: She has long, dark hair.
It's a long drive from Boston to Miami.

senses.def: lasting or taking a lot of time
examples: It's been a long day — I'm exhausted.
We had to wait a long time for the bus.

senses.def: for a long time
examples: Have you been waiting long?
It won't take long to fix the problem.

senses.def: to want something very much
examples: After weeks of rain, we were longing for some sunshine.

note: "As long as" = provided that (yeter ki). "No longer" = not anymore. In questions/negatives, use "long"; in positive sentences, "a long time".

senses.tr: köklü, uzun süredir var olan, eskiye dayanan
senses.def: having existed or lasted for a long time
examples: The two companies have a long-standing partnership.
The decision ended a long-standing dispute over land rights.

note: Usually describes relationships, problems or traditions, not people. For people, use "long-time".

senses.def: lasting or having an effect over a long period of time
examples: Smoking has serious long-term effects on your health.
We need a long-term solution, not a quick fix.

senses.def: over a long period of time
examples: Investing in education pays off long-term.

note: Opposite: short-term. "In the long term" (British) = "in the long run" (American, more common).

senses.def: having been a particular thing for a long time
examples: She married her long-time boyfriend last summer.
He's a long-time resident of the neighborhood.

note: Often written "longtime" in American English. Used before nouns describing people.

senses.def: to turn your eyes toward someone or something so you can see them
examples: Look at this photo of the kids at the beach.
She looked out the window at the rain.

senses.def: to seem or appear to be something
examples: You look tired — did you sleep well?
It looks like it's going to snow.

senses.def: to try to find someone or something
examples: I'm looking for my car keys.

senses.def: an act of looking at something, or someone's appearance
examples: Can I take a look at your notes?
I don't like the look of that cut — see a doctor.

note: "Look forward to" + -ing: I look forward to meeting you. "Look after" = take care of.

senses.def: to appear as a large, unclear shape, especially in a frightening way
examples: A huge ship loomed out of the fog.
Dark storm clouds loomed over the hills.

senses.def: to seem likely to happen soon, especially something bad
examples: With exams looming, students packed the library.
A trade war is looming between the two countries.

senses.def: a machine for weaving cloth
examples: The village women still weave rugs on wooden looms.

note: "Loom large" = seem very important or worrying.

senses.def: a shape like a circle made by a line curving round, or a piece of string in this shape
examples: Tie a loop at the end of the rope.
The road makes a loop around the lake.

senses.def: a process or series of events that keeps repeating
examples: The song was playing on a loop all afternoon.

senses.def: to make a loop or move in a circular path
examples: He looped the cable around the post.

note: "Keep me in the loop" = keep me informed. A "loophole" is a gap in a law that lets people avoid it.

senses.def: not firmly fixed in place
examples: One of the screws on the chair is loose.
My son has a loose tooth.

senses.def: not fitting tightly
examples: Wear loose, comfortable clothes for the yoga class.

senses.def: free to move around, not tied up or kept somewhere
examples: A dangerous dog is loose in the neighborhood.
The prisoner is still on the loose.

note: Don't confuse "loose" /luːs/ (gevşek) with "lose" /luːz/ (kaybetmek). "Loose ends" = unfinished details.

senses.def: a man of high rank in the British nobility, or a man with power in medieval times
examples: The castle belonged to a wealthy lord.
In the Middle Ages, peasants worked the land for their lord.

senses.def: a title for God or Jesus Christ
examples: They prayed to the Lord for help.
Oh Lord, I forgot my passport!

note: "Good Lord!" and "Oh Lord!" express surprise. A "drug lord" is a powerful drug trafficker.

senses.def: (British) a large vehicle for carrying heavy goods by road
examples: A lorry carrying fruit overturned on the motorway.
The lorry driver had been on the road for ten hours.

note: British only. In American English, say "truck" (and "semi" or "tractor-trailer" for a tır).

senses.def: to be unable to find something, or to stop having something
examples: I always lose my keys somewhere in the house.
Thousands of workers will lose their jobs when the factory closes.

senses.def: to be defeated in a game, competition or election
examples: Our team hates to lose at home.
If we lose this game, we're out of the tournament.

senses.def: to have less of something, such as weight, time or money
examples: He wants to lose ten pounds before summer.

note: Irregular: lose – lost – lost. Pronounced /luːz/; don't confuse with "loose" /luːs/.

senses.def: the state of no longer having something or having less of it
examples: The storm caused a loss of power across the city.
Memory loss can be an early sign of disease.

senses.def: money that a business loses
examples: The airline reported a loss of $200 million this quarter.

senses.def: the death of someone, or a defeat in a game
examples: We were saddened by the loss of our friend.
It was the team's third loss in a row.

note: "Be at a loss (for words)" = not know what to say or do. "I'm sorry for your loss" is said to someone grieving.

senses.def: unable to find your way, or unable to be found
examples: We got lost on the way to the hotel.
The airline is still searching for my lost luggage.

senses.def: confused or not knowing what to do
examples: I was completely lost in the first math class.
She felt lost after her husband died.

note: "Get lost!" is a rude way to tell someone to go away. "Lost and found" = kayıp eşya bürosu.

senses.def: a large number or amount
examples: I learned a lot from my first job.
There's a lot to do before the guests arrive.

senses.tr: (a lot of / lots of) çok, birçok
senses.def: a large number or amount of
examples: She has a lot of friends in the city.
We spent lots of money on the wedding.

senses.def: very much or very often
examples: I feel a lot better today.
We go to the beach a lot in summer.

senses.def: an area of land used for a particular purpose
examples: I parked in the lot behind the supermarket.

note: "A lot" is two words, never "alot". "Parking lot" is American; British say "car park".

senses.def: a game where people buy numbered tickets and prizes go to those whose numbers are chosen by chance
examples: He quit his job after winning the lottery.
She buys a lottery ticket every week.

senses.def: a situation whose result depends only on luck
examples: Getting a spot in that school is a bit of a lottery.

note: "Win the lottery" also means to be extremely lucky in general.

senses.def: making a lot of noise
examples: The music at the party was too loud to talk.
There was a loud bang from the kitchen.

senses.def: too bright or colorful
examples: He wore a loud Hawaiian shirt to the funeral.

senses.def: in a way that makes a lot of noise
examples: Could you speak a little louder? I can't hear you.

note: "Read out loud" = read aloud (sesli okumak). "Loud and clear" = clearly understood.

senses.def: in a way that makes a lot of noise
examples: The baby was crying loudly in the next room.
He complained loudly about the slow service.

senses.def: a very strong feeling of caring for someone, or of romantic attraction
examples: Their love for each other grew stronger over the years.
She fell in love with her best friend.

senses.def: to have very strong feelings of caring for someone
examples: I love you more than anything.
Parents love their children unconditionally.

senses.def: to like something very much
examples: I love Italian food.
She loves going to concerts.

senses.def: something that you enjoy very much
examples: Music was his first love.

note: "I'd love to" is a warm way to accept an invitation. In tennis, "love" means zero.

senses.def: beautiful or attractive
examples: You look lovely in that dress.
They have a lovely house by the lake.

senses.def: very pleasant or enjoyable
examples: We had a lovely evening — thanks for inviting us.
It's a lovely day for a picnic.

note: More common in British English; Americans often say "great", "beautiful" or "wonderful" instead.

senses.def: not high or tall; close to the ground
examples: Mind your head — the ceiling is very low.
The sun was low in the sky.

senses.def: below the usual level, amount or value
examples: The store sells clothes at very low prices.
My phone battery is low.

senses.def: in or into a low position or level
examples: The plane flew low over the houses.

senses.def: a low level or point
examples: The stock fell to a record low on Monday.

note: "Feel low" = feel sad. "Keep a low profile" = avoid attracting attention.

senses.def: to reduce something in amount, value or level
examples: The bank lowered interest rates for the second time this year.
Regular exercise helps lower blood pressure.

senses.def: to move something to a lower position
examples: The workers lowered the piano carefully down the stairs.
She lowered her voice so nobody else could hear.

senses.def: located below something else of the same type
examples: The cleaning supplies are on the lower shelf.

note: Opposite: raise. "Lower yourself" (to do something) = do something beneath your dignity.

senses.def: always supporting a person, organization or belief
examples: He has been a loyal friend for over twenty years.
The brand has many loyal customers.

senses.def: the quality of always supporting someone or something
examples: The company rewards customer loyalty with discounts.
Dogs are known for their loyalty to their owners.

senses.def: good or bad things that happen by chance and not because of your own actions
examples: Good luck with your interview tomorrow!
We've had a lot of bad luck with this car.

senses.def: success or good things that happen by chance
examples: I've had no luck finding an apartment so far.
With any luck, we'll be home by six.

note: "Good luck!" is said before a challenge. "Tough luck" can sound unsympathetic.

senses.def: having good luck, or happening because of good luck
examples: You're lucky to have such a supportive family.
It was a lucky guess — I didn't really know the answer.

senses.def: believed to bring good luck
examples: Seven is my lucky number.

senses.def: a meal eaten in the middle of the day
examples: Let's have lunch together on Friday.
I usually eat lunch at my desk.

note: No article in general use: "have lunch", not "have a lunch". "Out to lunch" (informal) can also mean crazy or unaware.

senses.def: either of the two organs in the chest used for breathing
examples: Smoking is the main cause of lung cancer.
The swimmer filled her lungs with air before diving.

collocations: at the top of your lungs
note: "At the top of your lungs" (American) = as loudly as possible.

senses.def: great comfort and pleasure from expensive and beautiful things
examples: They live in luxury in a huge villa.
The hotel offers every luxury you can imagine.

senses.def: something pleasant but expensive or not necessary
examples: A long, quiet bath is a real luxury for parents of young kids.

senses.def: expensive and of very high quality
examples: They spent their honeymoon in a luxury resort.

senses.def: the words of a song (usually plural)
examples: I love the melody, but I can never remember the lyrics.
She wrote the lyrics for the band's latest album.

senses.def: expressing personal feelings in a poetic, song-like way
examples: The book contains her best lyric poetry.

senses.def: a piece of equipment with moving parts that does a particular job
examples: The washing machine broke down again.
Can you get me a soda from the vending machine?

senses.def: an organized group of people who control something, especially in politics
examples: The party's political machine worked hard to win the election.

senses.def: machines as a group, especially large ones
examples: The factory invested in new farm machinery.
Heavy machinery is used to clear the site.

senses.def: the organization or system for doing something
examples: The machinery of government moves slowly.

note: Uncountable: "a piece of machinery", not "a machinery".

senses.def: very angry (informal, especially American)
examples: My mom was mad at me for coming home so late.
Don't get mad — it was just a joke.

senses.def: very silly or not sensible; mentally ill (old-fashioned)
examples: You'd be mad to turn down that job offer.
It was a mad idea to drive all night.

senses.def: very enthusiastic about something (informal)
examples: He's mad about baseball.

note: In American English, "mad" usually means angry. Calling a person mentally ill "mad" is offensive.

senses.def: a thin publication with articles and photos, sold weekly or monthly, or a similar online publication
examples: I read a fashion magazine while waiting at the dentist.
She writes for a popular science magazine.

note: Trap: "magazine" is not "mağaza" (store). In American English, the stress is often on the first syllable.

senses.def: the secret power of making impossible things happen by using special words or actions
examples: In the story, the witch uses magic to turn the prince into a frog.
The kids loved the magic show at the party.

senses.def: a special, exciting quality that makes something seem wonderful
examples: Nothing beats the magic of Christmas morning.

senses.def: having or using special powers to make impossible things happen
examples: There's no magic solution to poverty.
Say the magic word!

note: "The magic word" (to children) = "please".

senses.def: containing or using magic
examples: The fairy tale is about a girl with magical powers.
Some plants were once believed to have magical properties.

senses.def: wonderful and exciting in a special way
examples: Our evening in Venice was absolutely magical.

senses.def: an official who acts as a judge in courts that deal with less serious cases
examples: The magistrate fined him $500 for disorderly conduct.
She appeared before a magistrate the morning after her arrest.

note: Formal and legal. In the US, magistrate judges assist federal judges; in the UK they hear minor cases.

senses.def: acting like a magnet, or able to be attracted by a magnet
examples: The Earth has a magnetic field that protects it from the sun.
Credit cards used to rely on a magnetic strip.

senses.def: having a quality that strongly attracts people
examples: The singer had a magnetic personality on stage.

senses.def: extremely beautiful, impressive or deserving praise
examples: From the top, there's a magnificent view of the canyon.
She gave a magnificent performance in the final.

senses.def: the great size or importance of something
examples: Nobody understood the magnitude of the problem at first.
A crisis of this magnitude requires international cooperation.

senses.def: the size or strength of an earthquake or a star's brightness
examples: A magnitude 7.2 earthquake struck the coast early this morning.

note: Formal. "An order of magnitude" = about ten times larger or smaller.

senses.def: the system for sending letters and packages, or the letters and packages sent
examples: I sent the documents by mail last week.
Has the mail come yet today?

senses.def: email
examples: I've got over a hundred unread messages in my mail.

senses.def: to send something by post
examples: Could you mail this package for me on your way to work?

note: American "mail" = British "post". Uncountable: "a lot of mail", not "mails" (for letters).

senses.def: largest or most important
examples: The main reason I moved was the job.
Turn left onto the main road.

senses.def: a large pipe or cable that carries water, gas or electricity to buildings
examples: A burst water main flooded the street.

note: Used only before nouns: "the main problem", not "the problem is main". "Main Street" also symbolizes ordinary Americans.

senses.def: the main area of land of a country or region, not including islands near it
examples: The ferry takes about an hour to reach the mainland.
Prices on the island are higher than on the mainland.

note: Almost always used with "the": the mainland.

senses.def: more than anything else; mostly
examples: The audience was mainly made up of students.
I use my phone mainly for messages and maps.

senses.tr: ana akım, genel kabul gören, yaygın
senses.def: considered normal because it is accepted by most people
examples: The band has never had much mainstream success.
Electric cars are becoming more mainstream every year.

senses.def: the ideas, opinions and styles shared by most people
examples: Yoga has moved from the fringe into the mainstream.

note: "Mainstream media" = large, traditional news organizations.

senses.def: to make something continue at the same level or standard
examples: It's important to maintain a healthy weight.
The two countries maintain close ties.

senses.def: to keep a building or machine in good condition by checking and repairing it
examples: The city spends millions to maintain its roads.

senses.def: to keep saying that something is true, even when others disagree
examples: He has always maintained his innocence.

note: Note the spelling change: maintain → maintenance (not "maintainance").

senses.def: the work of keeping something in good condition by checking and repairing it
examples: The elevator is closed for maintenance.
Older cars need more regular maintenance.

senses.def: the act of making a situation or state continue
examples: The UN plays a role in the maintenance of world peace.

note: "High-maintenance" (informal) describes a person who needs a lot of attention.

senses.def: very large, important or serious
examples: Traffic is a major problem in the city.
The surgery was a major operation.

senses.def: the main subject a student studies at college, or a student studying it (American)
examples: Her major is biology.
He's an English major at Ohio State.

senses.def: to study something as your main subject at college (American)
examples: I majored in economics.

note: Opposite: minor. "Major" is also a military rank (binbaşı).

senses.def: the largest part of a group of people or things
examples: The majority of students live on campus.
A large majority of voters support the plan.

senses.def: the number of votes by which one party or candidate wins
examples: The party won the election with a majority of 30 seats.

note: "The majority of" + plural noun takes a plural verb: The majority of people are...

senses.def: to create or prepare something by putting materials or parts together
examples: I'll make dinner tonight.
This company makes furniture from recycled wood.

senses.def: to cause or force someone to do something
examples: Sad movies always make me cry.
My parents made me practice piano every day.

senses.def: to earn money, or to add up to a total
examples: She makes about $80,000 a year.
Two and two make four.

senses.def: the name of the company that made a product
examples: What make is your car?

note: Irregular: make – made – made. "Make someone do" (no "to"). Turks often confuse make/do: make a mistake, do homework.

senses.def: colored substances put on the face to look more attractive or to change your appearance
examples: She never wears much make-up to work.
The actors spent two hours in make-up before the show.

senses.def: the different parts or people that form something, or a person's character
examples: The ethnic make-up of the city has changed a lot.
Being competitive is part of his genetic make-up.

note: Usually spelled "makeup" in American English. Uncountable: "a lot of makeup". The verb "make up" also means invent or reconcile.
